correctness.rationale: All n+1 Sturmian words yield distinct occupied image atoms, by published minimality and atom-language lemma. Each has diameter at most lambda^n. The two first-step image intervals have exact gap 1-lambda; induction on the common terminal branch yields an inter-atom gap at least (1-lambda)lambda^{n-1}. These independent upper and lower cover bounds force N_K(r)=log(1/r)/log(1/lambda)+O_lambda(1). Endpoint closures and strict inequalities do not affect the asymptotic. Finite checker is supplementary.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The broader zero-dimension result is strictly weaker: e.g., disparate sublogarithmic coverings still have zero box dimension. It does not imply the sharp coefficient without the new lower separation proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new theorem uses known input count n+1 and similarity ratio, but requires an additional, uniformly positive separation of distinct n-atoms at scale (1-lambda)lambda^{n-1}. This supplies the missing matching lower bound for minimal interval coverings. A trivial restatement of the dimension-zero theorem cannot imply the coefficient.

value.rationale: The sharp nonzero logarithmic covering coefficient quantifies metric size invisible to the known vanishing ordinary Hausdorff and box dimensions. Its independence from irrational rotation number is a natural universality statement across an established Cantor attractor family; the coefficient is useful for resolution complexity and approximation of invariant sets.
